question: Can an arbitrary image model trained only on a canonical data distribution be wrapped at inference time with energy-based diffeomorphic registration so that segmentation becomes approximately equivariant and topology classification approximately invariant under unseen image warps, without retraining the task model on augmented data?

key_findings.claim: DiffeoNN extends energy canonicalization from finite-dimensional Lie-group descent to image deformations represented by stationary velocity fields, while leaving the inner task network unchanged.
key_findings.evidence: For each input x, a SIREN parameterizes a stationary velocity field v; scaling and squaring produces g_x=exp(v), and gradient descent minimizes a data-similarity plus deformation-regularity energy. The canonical image g_x dot x is passed through the already trained inner network. For segmentation, the predicted mask is warped back by g_x inverse; for classification the output action is trivial. The image energy combines a VAE reconstruction term and an adversarial discriminator trained to distinguish original from randomly deformed training images, while the deformation energy penalizes velocity gradients and negative Jacobian determinants.

key_findings.claim: The wrapper is not exactly equivariant to the full diffeomorphism group in the implemented method; its guarantee is conditional and approximate.
key_findings.evidence: Section 2 states exact equivariance only if the canonicalization energy obeys E_can(h dot x,g)=E_can(x,g composed with h). Section 3.2 explicitly says adding E_reg violates this condition, and Section 3.3 says finite-step optimization makes exact minimizers inaccessible. The search space is only stationary-velocity-field exponentials; the authors note not every orientation-preserving diffeomorphism is generated by an SVF. Moreover, this SVF-exponential set is closed under inversion but is not established as closed under composition, so it is not the full group used by the exact theorem.

key_findings.claim: On 100 synthetically warped nested-square images, DiffeoNN materially improves the unaugmented U-Net but remains below the augmented U-Net on every mean segmentation metric.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1a reports naive/DiffeoNN/augmented IoU 0.9276/0.9571/0.9770, Dice 0.9582/0.9777/0.9878, and pixel accuracy 0.9962/0.9981/0.9989. Thus DiffeoNN closes 59.5% of the naive-to-augmentation IoU gap but retains a 0.0199 absolute IoU deficit to augmentation. Box plots show fewer or smaller low-Dice outliers for DiffeoNN than the naive model, but no numerical dispersion or uncertainty is reported.

key_findings.claim: On 60 synthetically warped chest X-rays, DiffeoNN's mean gain over the naive U-Net is small and augmentation remains clearly better.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1b reports naive/DiffeoNN/augmented IoU 0.8759/0.8842/0.9231, Dice 0.9295/0.9327/0.9594, and accuracy 0.9729/0.9746/0.9836. DiffeoNN therefore gains only 0.0083 IoU over naive and closes 17.6% of the naive-to-augmentation IoU gap, while trailing augmentation by 0.0389. The images are transformed test samples from a 234/60/60 train/validation/test split, not a naturally occurring external deformation cohort.

anchors.section: Appendix B: Visual Results: Lung Segmentation

key_findings.claim: On 100 diffeomorphically transformed MNIST images classified by genus, DiffeoNN improves the naive classifier and ties augmentation in reported mean accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1c reports accuracy 0.68 for naive and 0.82 for both DiffeoNN and the augmented classifier. The appendix shows individual successes and failures, but the study has one 100-image transformed sample, no repeat seeds, no confidence interval, and no evaluation of ordinary digit identity because that label is not invariant to the paper's broad diffeomorphism class.

anchors.section: Appendix C: Results: Homology Classification on MNIST

key_findings.claim: The experiments demonstrate improvement on new samples from the training deformation generator, not generalization to an unseen transformation family or to the full diffeomorphism group.
key_findings.evidence: The transformed evaluation sets are produced by sampling radial-basis-function deformation parameters, and the adversarial energy is trained on original images versus on-the-fly random diffeomorphisms described as similar to those used to create the transformed test set. The paper does not hold out deformation basis families, magnitudes, spatial frequencies, nonstationary flows, scanner or patient domains, or real longitudinal anatomical changes. 'Unseen transformations' therefore means unseen sampled instances from a matched synthetic generator.

anchors.section: Appendix A.2 Experiments on the Synthetic Dataset

key_findings.claim: The appendix documents a causal failure chain: failed canonicalization produces artifacts that are inherited by the final segmentation, and good-looking canonicalization cannot rescue an inadequate inner model.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 7 row five shows a failed canonicalization whose artifacts propagate through segmentation and reverse warping. Figure 10 shows lung cases where DiffeoNN and the naive model have gaps or missing parts and augmentation is usually more accurate. Figure 11 shows images whose canonical forms look close to training data but all three task models still miss the ground truth, demonstrating that orbit alignment cannot supply task knowledge absent from the inner model.

key_findings.claim: The paper does not directly measure the quantity in its title: equivariance error over paired transformations.
key_findings.evidence: The primary metrics are downstream IoU, Dice, pixel accuracy, and classification accuracy. Figure 5 compares four pairs visually and says their post-canonicalization energies are approximately equal, but there is no distribution of ||f_tilde(h dot x)-h dot f_tilde(x)||, no composition-consistency test, no inverse-consistency metric, and no residual versus deformation magnitude. A task-score improvement can occur without uniform approximate equivariance and does not test the full transformation set.

key_findings.claim: Claims of data and compute efficiency are unquantified and omit the wrapper's training and per-input optimization costs.
key_findings.evidence: The method avoids augmented retraining of the inner task model, but it trains a VAE and adversarial discriminator for each domain and optimizes a SIREN/SVF for each input; lung and MNIST use 100 canonicalization gradient steps. No end-to-end training time, inference latency, memory, energy, augmented-sample count, or labeled-data scaling curve is reported. Calling augmentation a theoretical performance ceiling is also too strong: a finite augmented model is an empirical baseline, and a different augmentation distribution or model could perform differently.

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence supports retrofitting small task networks trained in the study, but not yet the broader claim that any arbitrary pretrained network can be made diffeomorphism-equivariant.
key_findings.evidence: The inner models are a simple U-Net trained for 10 epochs on aligned synthetic squares, a U-Net trained on the study's original chest X-rays, and a simple convolutional genus classifier trained on MNIST. Each domain also supplies the canonical training images used to train the energy models. There is no frozen off-the-shelf foundation model, no architecture diversity, no unavailable-training-data scenario, and no output space with a nontrivial action beyond 2D masks.

key_findings.claim: The Jacobian penalty encourages but does not guarantee orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms in the discretized implementation.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 11 penalizes max(0,-det J_g), which is zero at determinant zero as well as positive determinant, and the paper supplies no minimum-Jacobian statistics, fold count, inverse-consistency error, or discretization analysis. A smooth continuous SVF flow is theoretically diffeomorphic under regularity assumptions, but a finite grid, learned SIREN, and numerical scaling-and-squaring implementation still require verification; the soft hinge is not itself a hard positivity constraint.

method.core_idea: At inference, register every input into the task network's familiar training-data orbit slice, apply the unchanged task model there, and transform structured outputs back; learn the registration energy from unlabeled canonical images and search a stationary-velocity-field deformation with gradient descent.
method.mechanism: A VAE reconstruction loss and adversarial discriminator score whether g dot x resembles the original training distribution X_E. A velocity-gradient penalty favors smooth fields, and a negative-Jacobian hinge discourages folds. A SIREN represents v, scaling and squaring approximates exp(v), and finite-step gradient descent minimizes E_can(x,g). The resulting x_c=g_x dot x enters f_theta. Segmentation returns g_x inverse dot f_theta(x_c); classification uses the trivial output action. The synthetic and real segmentation inner models are U-Nets, while MNIST genus uses a convolutional classifier. Domain-specific VAE/discriminator weights and 100-step canonicalization are selected manually in the appendices.
assumptions: The relevant domain shift is well modeled by an orientation-preserving spatial diffeomorphism that preserves the task label or transforms the output mask by the same action.
Every test input's orbit intersects a region close enough to X_E for the inner model to work.
The VAE and discriminator assign lower energy to useful canonical representatives rather than merely high-density or easily reconstructed but task-distorting images.
A stationary velocity field is expressive enough for the deformations of interest even though not every orientation-preserving diffeomorphism is an SVF exponential.
Finite-grid scaling and squaring and the Jacobian hinge yield an invertible, orientation-preserving transformation with an accurate inverse.
The nonconvex energy can be optimized from the chosen initialization in a finite number of per-input steps and harmful local minima are rare.
Nonunique low-energy canonical representatives are equivalent enough for the task model, though the paper leaves formal validation open.
Breaking the exact energy transformation law with deformation regularization introduces negligible equivariance error.
The adversarial deformations used to train the energy cover the test deformation distribution without leaking the specific test samples.
The output group action is known and executable; reverse warping is meaningful for segmentation and the action is truly trivial for genus classification.
Interpolation during forward and inverse image/mask warps does not materially change topology, boundaries, or evaluation metrics.
Training the VAE and discriminator and optimizing 100 steps per input is cheaper or more practical than augmenting or retraining the task model.
Performance on 100/60/100 matched transformed samples represents behavior under a broad, infinite-dimensional transformation family.
The canonical training images remain available for adapting an arbitrary pretrained network.

techniques.role: Selects a low-energy representative from an input's deformation orbit before task inference.
Represents a tractable subset of smooth invertible spatial deformations with a SIREN velocity field.
Numerically exponentiates the stationary velocity field and obtains an inverse by negating the field.
Uses reconstruction/latent fit to score whether a warped input resembles the canonical training distribution.
Trains a discriminator on original versus randomly deformed images to sharpen the canonical-data score.
Penalizes spatial variation in the velocity field and negative deformation Jacobians.
Optimizes a new canonicalizing transformation for each test input rather than predicting one in a single feed-forward pass.
Warps a canonical segmentation back to the input coordinates, converting invariant preprocessing into an approximately equivariant wrapper.
Evaluates original-data task models on held-out images warped by sampled radial-basis deformations.
Shows both optimizer failures and inner-model failures so the two sources of error can be distinguished.

limitations: Author-stated: the regularizing energy violates the transformation condition needed for strict canonicalization equivariance.
Author-stated: finite-step numerical optimization cannot reach exact minimizers, so canonicalization is only approximately invariant.
Author-stated: not every orientation-preserving diffeomorphism can be generated by a stationary velocity field.
Author-stated: the canonicalization energy is nonconvex and its minimizer need not be unique; formal justification that any low-energy representative suffices is left to future work.
Author-stated in the conclusion: stability, generalization bounds, and conditions under which approximate canonicalization yields full-model equivariance remain open.
Reviewer-identified: D_SVF is not shown to be closed under composition, while the exact equivariance argument assumes a group.
Reviewer-identified: the negative-Jacobian hinge does not enforce strict positivity and no fold, minimum-determinant, or inverse-consistency statistics are reported.
Reviewer-identified: all test warps come from a deformation family matched to the adversarial-energy training generator; there is no out-of-generator transformation test.
Reviewer-identified: no direct paired equivariance residual is measured, so downstream task gains do not establish approximate equivariance over the claimed action.
Reviewer-identified: augmentation beats DiffeoNN on all mean synthetic and lung metrics and ties it on MNIST; robustness from 'fewer outliers' is not quantified.
Reviewer-identified: samples are small (100 synthetic, 60 lung, 100 MNIST), with no repeat seeds, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, or external datasets.
Reviewer-identified: the lung experiment applies synthetic warps to one dataset rather than testing real anatomical, scanner, institution, or disease shift.
Reviewer-identified: data-efficiency claims lack labeled-data scaling curves and exact augmented-set sizes.
Reviewer-identified: compute-efficiency claims omit VAE/discriminator training, per-input 100-step optimization, wall-clock latency, memory, and energy.
Reviewer-identified: energy weights, latent size, and canonicalization steps change by task without sensitivity analysis or a validation-selection protocol.
Reviewer-identified: no ablation isolates VAE, adversarial, smoothness, or Jacobian terms.
Reviewer-identified: experiments train each inner task model specifically for the study and do not test diverse or off-the-shelf pretrained backbones.

Reviewer-identified: v1 promises source code only 'upon publication,' so the exact deformation sampler, initialization, interpolation, and optimizer are not reproducible from the archived paper alone.
failure_modes: The optimizer converges to a low-energy but task-wrong canonical representative because image likelihood and task sufficiency are not the same objective.
A test warp lies outside the stationary-flow or training-generator support, leaving the canonical image out of distribution.
Nonconvex descent stalls or becomes initialization-sensitive within the fixed 100-step budget.
The VAE favors blurry reconstructions or the discriminator exploits superficial texture, causing anatomically incorrect registration.
The negative-Jacobian soft penalty permits zero or discretely folded regions and reverse warping corrupts masks.
Repeated interpolation erodes thin structures, changes boundary topology, or inflates apparent pixel accuracy on background-heavy images.
Regularization prefers a small deformation even when a larger valid deformation is required, breaking orbit consistency.
Two transformed versions of the same image reach different local minima, producing a large equivariance residual despite similar energies.
The inner model is wrong on the canonical image, so perfect registration cannot recover the correct label or segmentation.
The output does not admit the assumed group action, or the action is ambiguous for structured labels beyond masks and topology classes.
Per-input optimization is too slow or memory-intensive for deployment, erasing any training-time savings over augmentation.
An augmented baseline trained with a better deformation distribution widens rather than closes the accuracy gap.
Natural medical variation includes intensity, pathology, occlusion, acquisition, and non-diffeomorphic changes that spatial canonicalization cannot remove.
A canonical training set is unavailable for a third-party pretrained model, preventing energy-model adaptation.
reusable_insights: A symmetry wrapper can be decomposed into canonicalize, infer, and inverse-transform stages, allowing a frozen task model to be reused.
Image registration supplies practical parameterizations and optimizers for transformation groups too large for group averaging.
Separate canonicalizer failures from inner-model failures with intermediate images and outputs; each requires a different remedy.
Measure the equivariance residual directly over paired transformations in addition to task accuracy.
Test deformation families, magnitudes, spatial frequencies, and compositions that are held out from both canonicalizer and augmentation training.
Report minimum Jacobian determinant, fold fraction, inverse consistency, and interpolation effects whenever a learned warp is called diffeomorphic.
An energy learned from unlabeled canonical examples can adapt a frozen predictor, but its training and inference cost must be counted.
Compare canonicalization with augmentation at matched data, compute, tuning, and wall-clock budgets rather than treating augmentation as an abstract ceiling.
Use task-aware or joint energy diagnostics to detect low-energy canonical forms that discard information the downstream predictor needs.
A soft deformation regularizer creates a deliberate accuracy-equivariance trade-off; quantify that trade instead of invoking exact group theory after the condition is broken.
open_questions: What is the distribution of paired equivariance residuals as deformation magnitude, frequency, and composition increase?
Does DiffeoNN generalize to deformation generators, time-dependent velocity fields, and real anatomical shifts excluded from energy training?
How often do scaling-and-squaring outputs contain nonpositive discrete Jacobians, and how accurate is exp(-v) as the numerical inverse?
Can multiple starts, amortized initialization, or a learned optimizer reduce local-minimum failures and 100-step latency?
Which energy components are necessary, and how sensitive are results to lambda_adv, lambda_VAE, lambda_Delta, lambda_J, latent dimension, and step count?
How do performance and total cost scale with labeled canonical data, unlabeled energy-training data, and augmented data?
Does the wrapper improve frozen off-the-shelf foundation models and architectures other than small CNNs and U-Nets?
Can a task-aware energy reject low-energy representatives on which the inner predictor is uncertain or wrong?
Would weighted frames or distributions over multiple canonical minima be more stable than one nonunique point estimate?
Can an exactly transformation-compatible regularizer retain physical plausibility without sacrificing the canonicalization identity?
How does DiffeoNN compare with Equivariant Adaptation, Improved Canonicalization, LieLAC, and DiffKillR under matched transformation sets and compute?
What output actions beyond binary masks and genus classification can be reversed reliably?
Are improvements preserved on multiclass pathology segmentation, thin structures, topology-sensitive masks, and 3D volumes?
When is per-input registration cheaper than retraining or augmentation over the lifetime of a deployed model?

competitive_landscape.title: Equivariance with Learned Canonicalization Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: Kaba et al. learn equivariant canonicalization functions that plug into ordinary backbones and establish universality across image, dynamics, and point-cloud tasks. DiffeoNN instead optimizes a per-input energy and specializes the transformation search to SVF image registration, targeting a much larger deformation family but losing exactness through regularization and finite descent.

competitive_landscape.title: Equivariant Adaptation of Large Pretrained Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Mondal et al. already adapt large frozen pretrained models with a canonicalization network and dataset-dependent priors so canonical orientations match the training distribution, evaluated for deterministic groups such as rotations. DiffeoNN's generic 'any pretrained network' framing is therefore prior art; its distinct contribution is the SVF/registration energy for approximate diffeomorphisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Improved Canonicalization for Model Agnostic Equivariance
competitive_landscape.difference: Panigrahi and Mondal use contrastive learning plus optimization with a non-equivariant canonicalization network, reporting model-agnostic adaptation of large pretrained models and up to 2x speedup. DiffeoNN instead learns a VAE/adversarial image energy and optimizes an SVF, enabling nonrigid spatial deformation but with no latency comparison.

competitive_landscape.title: Lie Algebra Canonicalization: Equivariant Neural Operators under arbitrary Lie Groups
competitive_landscape.difference: LieLAC performs energy canonicalization by descent in finite-dimensional Lie algebras and retrofits pretrained image classifiers and PDE operators. DiffeoNN explicitly extends this recipe to stationary velocity fields, adds image-registration regularizers, and reverses the warp for segmentation; that infinite-dimensional image-deformation specialization is the clearest incremental novelty.

competitive_landscape.title: Equivariant Frames and the Impossibility of Continuous Canonicalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Dym et al. show that continuous deterministic canonicalization or unweighted frames can be impossible for common group actions and construct weighted frames that preserve continuity. DiffeoNN uses a nonunique deterministic argmin and empirically tolerates discontinuity/local minima, but supplies no continuity or stability analysis for its diffeomorphism action.

competitive_landscape.title: DiffKillR: Killing and Recreating Diffeomorphisms for Cell Annotation in Dense Microscopy Images
competitive_landscape.difference: DiffKillR learns diffeomorphism-invariant cell matching and a separate registration field to propagate pixel annotations from a small archetype library in microscopy. DiffeoNN is a more generic frozen-model wrapper based on energy minimization and tests lung/synthetic segmentation plus topology classification, but DiffKillR predates the broad claim that registration plus invariance can reduce annotation needs under diffeomorphisms.

competitive_landscape.title: A Canonicalization Perspective on Invariant and Equivariant Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Ma et al. characterize connections and complexity relations between canonical forms and frame averaging and design optimal frames for selected actions. DiffeoNN contributes an applied registration construction for image diffeomorphisms, but its claim of a broader theoretical gap should be narrowed because substantial canonicalization theory already exists even if full infinite-dimensional SVF guarantees remain open.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim to extend energy canonicalization to the infinite-dimensional group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, make any pretrained network diffeomorphism-equivariant without retraining or extensive augmentation, and obtain robust, data-efficient generalization to unseen transformations through SVF-based differentiable registration.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Learned canonicalization, frozen pretrained-model adaptation, optimization-based model-agnostic canonicalization, and canonicalization/frame theory are all established by Kaba et al., Equivariant Adaptation, Improved Canonicalization, LieLAC, Dym et al., and Ma et al. LieLAC is the explicit closest predecessor. DiffKillR already combines diffeomorphism-invariant matching and registration for pixel annotation. DiffeoNN uniquely assembles a VAE/adversarial training-manifold energy, SVF/SIREN registration, deformation penalties, and inverse output warping for matched 2D deformation tests.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The credible novelty is an applied extension of LieLAC-style energy canonicalization to a tractable subset of image diffeomorphisms using differentiable registration, with a useful inverse-warp wrapper for segmentation. It is not the first generic canonicalization method for pretrained models, not exact equivariance, and not coverage of the full diffeomorphism group. Because the augmented baseline wins both segmentation means, the present evidence supports a modular no-task-retraining trade-off rather than superior accuracy, robustness, or compute efficiency.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 pages of arXiv v1 end to end, including the synthetic setup, lung and MNIST appendices, all Table 1 cells, and the explicit failure Figures 7 and 10-11. Source hashes and 17-page extraction coverage match fulltext_index. Author-reported metrics reproduce the paper; gap-closure arithmetic, matched-generator analysis, group/guarantee scope, cost accounting, and contradiction audits are reviewer inferences. Competitor titles, mechanisms, current versions, and dates were checked against official arXiv primary records on 2026-08-23 through mechanism/task, baseline/evaluation, and novelty/predecessor query families; two especially direct pretrained-canonicalization papers omitted by the target were added. Confidence is below verified because there is no independent second reviewer, code was unavailable in v1, and the paper reports no seeds or direct equivariance-residual data.
